brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
A roasted grain drink made from highland tartary buckwheat grown around Liupanshui in western Guizhou. It contains no tea leaf and takes the name only because it is steeped like tea.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
name_ru: Лю Пань Шуй Ку Цяо Ча
history: Linked to the practice of the local Yi people, it received national geographical indication protection on 1 December 2014, covering Liuzhi, Pan County, Shuicheng and Zhongshan. Buckwheat itself appears in the Compendium of Materia Medica. Little more is documented about the drink's own past.
processing: Highland tartary buckwheat is roasted by a traditional method; the steeped grains can be chewed afterwards.
harvest_season: Depends on the plant and the place.
taste_profile: Strong toasted-grain aroma of buckwheat with a scorched edge that lingers.
vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
